Why is the Beard discriminated against by so many? time after time I've been told by people to shave my Beard from family members outright saying it to staff at the unemployment office subtly suggesting it (thankfully i'm now employed by a beard friendly employer). Why are Beards treated so unfairly?

I wonder this too. I was speaking to a job recruiter once (many years ago) and he told me that I needed to shave off my beard if I expected to get a job. He said that simply having a beard could mean the difference between having to in for 5 interviews and having to go in for 50.

That's really fucking stupid.
I guess I can partially understand if it was for say hospitality (though thats what nets are for) but I was applying for administration jobs ffs.

I worked in customer service for a long while with a beard. If anything, it actually seemed to make people more relaxed/calm. It was like they saw this bearded guy (me) and decided I was going to handle their problem. It worked out well.

I vaguely remember reading somewhere that it has to do with all the soldiers in WWII needing to be clean shaven. When they came back and entered the business world that was the norm and that culture persists to this day.

I think a lot of it is regional. Where I'm from, in the mountains of Virginia, it seems like almost every man has some kind of facial hair. There is no discrimination. Applying for a job with a beard is not that big of deal. The big deal is the lack of jobs.

I get this too often. My mother nearly disowned me for growing my beard out. I started growing it early. Senior year, my high school demanded I shave because it was "unsanitary," which was rubbish. I'm 22 now, and I feel that people are intimidated by me. I'm 6'4" with long hair and the beard of Paul Bunyan. I'm the friendliest person, and nothing to be feared. Now that I'm a commentator, this beard is my persona. I've made it mine, and its going to the grave with me if I can help it.

I am the only one in my family with a full beard, and I get nothing but rude comments about it when we have family gatherings. Luckily I only have to put up with it for a few hours 2-3 times a year, but its still annoying as hell. Even more annoying when I go out in public and people comment on it telling me I look like a dirty hobo. I guess it just comes with the lifestyle choice of having my manliness leak out of my face.

Found this article which made the most sense, but in cliff notes, the beard fell out of style due to the increase of chemical agents being used during WWI where soldiers were forced to shave to ensure a good seal while using a gas mask.

Which correlates with the large portion of the population drafted into both wars, and those returning carrying on the habits that were developed during their service. The services were made to brush their teeth during WW2 and it carried on once they were released from service, making dental hygiene a daily habit, the same goes for shaving.
